domain:
Process Description – Care Allowance

The citizen begins by starting application.  Then the citizen needs to submit the information, including the child's age, medical certificate from the specialist and the number of caregivers. Once all information is submitted, the system robots must determine the fact: it must determine whether the age is minor, it must verify the certificate using the verification system, and it must check the child's national insurance membership. All of the above steps needs to be done once.
Based on the robots precheck, the following  rejection consequences are produced:
	• If the certificate is fake, the caseworker must reject it and must not approve it.
	• If the child doesn't have the national insurance membership, the caseworker must reject it and must not approve it.


Once the robot's precheck are passed, the caseworker must manually assess the criteria.

If the child is adult:
	• The caseworker will assess whether the child has developmental disability
	• The caseworker will assess whether the child need continuous supervision (life-threatening case) and care

Otherwise:
	• The caseworker must assess whether the child has illness or disability
	• The caseworker must assess whether the child needs continuous supervision

Moreover, 
	• The caseworker needs to determine whether care requires caregiver absent from work
	• If the citizen input number of caregiver more than 1 during submission, the caseworker must determine whether the care needs justifies a second caregivers.


Once all of the manual assessment is done, if any of the applicable conditions fails, the caseworker will reject it. Otherwise, the caseworker will grant the care allowance.
Additionally, during assessing the criteria, the caseworker must open a case after the robot precheck finishes. After the caseworker open the case, can assess criteria can happen.
Moreover, after the caseworker opened case, he can ask for both similar cases and relevant law. Then the system robot must find the similar cases or relevant laws. Once the finding is complete, the caseworker must review the similar cases or review relevant laws.
During reviewing information of both similar cases or relevant law, the manually assessing the information is blocked until the review is finished. And it also blocks the grant decision as well. 
When grant decision is finished,  the robot must summarize the case and the caseworker must issues assessment and justification after the robot summarization. Until then, the citizen can see the justification after issuing.

entries.text: propose some entities and roles

I have two options for the roles and entities.

**Roles (both options):** Citizen, Caseworker, Robot (the system robots) and Verification_System.

**Option 1, Core (recommended):** two entities, Application and Case.
- Application holds the submitted information and the prechecks.
- Case is what the caseworker opens to assess, review and decide.
- Similar cases, relevant law and the justification stay out for now. They can become actions or data properties later.

**Option 2, Fuller set:** adds four more entities: Certificate, Similar_Cases, Relevant_Law and Justification. It models more detail, but some of these may turn out to be only data.

Both plans pass the check. The entities are empty for now, and actions, properties and states come in later steps.

tools.arguments: {"options": [{"label": "Core roles and entities", "change": "Add roles Citizen, Caseworker, Robot (system robots), and Verification_System. Add entities Application (the care allowance application, holding submitted info), Case (opened by caseworker, for assessment and review), Similar_Cases and Relevant_Law is NOT needed. Keep it minimal: entities Application and Case only; roles Citizen, Caseworker, Robot, Verification_System. Entities declared empty (no actions, properties or states yet).", "recommended": true}, {"label": "Fuller set", "change": "Add roles Citizen, Caseworker, Robot, Verification_System. Add entities Application, Case, Certificate, Similar_Cases, Relevant_Law, Justification, each empty for now.", "recommended": false}]}

entries.text: Propose the data properties first.

I have two options for the data properties. Both pass the check.

**Core data properties (recommended):** eight properties.
- **Application:**
  - child_age (int)
  - number_of_caregivers (int)
  - medical_certificate (string)
  - is_minor (boolean)
  - certificate_valid (boolean)
  - has_insurance_membership (boolean)
- **Case:**
  - second_caregiver_justified (boolean)
  - all_criteria_met (boolean)

**Submission and prechecks only:** the six Application properties above, with nothing on Case.

The robot's prechecks and the "more than 1 caregiver" rule depend on these values, which is why I chose them. I left out the manual assessment results, such as disability or supervision need. They can be added later if the rules need them.

Add to entity Case: second_caregiver_justified: boolean, all_criteria_met: boolean. Only these, no states or actions.", "recommended": true}, {"label": "Submission and prechecks only", "change": "Add data properties to entity Application only: child_age: int, number_of_caregivers: int, medical_certificate: string, is_minor: boolean, certificate_valid: boolean, has_insurance_membership: boolean.", "recommended": false}]}

entries.text: Propose the actions for the application and robot precheck stage.

I have one option for this stage. It adds five actions to Application, each with an action specification, and the plan passes the check.

- **start_application:** the Citizen starts it, and it is available at the start.
- **submit_information:** the Citizen enters child_age, medical_certificate and number_of_caregivers as inputs.
- **determine_minor:** the Robot decides whether the child is a minor, with is_minor as its output.
- **verify_certificate:** the Robot checks the certificate, and Verification_System observes it. Its output is certificate_valid.
- **check_insurance_membership:** the Robot checks insurance, with has_insurance_membership as its output.

The order of these actions, for example submit_information only after start_application, and each robot step only once, comes later as enabled specifications. The actions after the precheck (rejection, assessment and so on) are a later batch.

No enabled specifications yet and no states.", "recommended": true}]}

entries.text: Propose the enabled specifications for the precheck actions.

I have one option for the precheck ordering. It adds four enabled specifications, and the plan passes the check.

- **submit_information:** enabled only after start_application was executed.
- **determine_minor, verify_certificate and check_insurance_membership:** each enabled only after submit_information was executed. The three robot steps can then run in any order.

The "done once" rule isn't covered by this plan. These conditions only set the order, so the robot steps could still repeat. A later action or scenario step could handle that.

entries.text: Propose the actions for rejection, opening the case and manual assessment.

I have two options. Both pass the check, and neither adds enabled specifications yet.

**Rejection and open case (recommended):** a small plan of three actions.
- **reject_fake_certificate** and **reject_no_insurance** go on Application. The Caseworker initiates them and the Citizen observes them.
- **open_case** goes on Case, initiated by the Caseworker.

**All including assessments:** the same three actions, plus six manual assessment actions on Case, all initiated by the Caseworker.
- assess_developmental_disability
- assess_life_threatening_supervision
- assess_illness_or_disability
- assess_continuous_supervision
- assess_caregiver_absence
- assess_second_caregiver

The two adult and minor assessment pairs are separate actions because the text names different criteria for each. Which pair applies depends on is_minor, and that comes later with the enabled specifications. The first option is about 10 elements, so it is easier to review. The second is larger, with 18 steps.

The revised plan is waiting for your approval. It differs from what you kept in two ways:

- **Decision inputs added:** each of the six assessment actions now takes a `decision: boolean` input from the Caseworker. This follows your reason that the assessment needs the caseworker's decision. The steps you kept had no inputs.
- **Reject actions left out:** both reject actions and their specifications stay out, as you asked.

The plan still adds `open_case` and the six assessment actions on Case, all initiated by the Caseworker. The check reports no problems.

I did not add the single reject action you mentioned, because it was not in what you kept. A single `reject_application` could be added in a later plan, initiated by the Caseworker and observed by the Citizen. Do you want that next?

`open_case` and the six assessment actions are now on Case. The Caseworker initiates all of them, and each assessment takes a `decision: boolean` input. The check reports no problems.

I suggest these next:
- **A single reject action,** as you described. It would cover both the precheck rejections and the final rejection.
- **Enabled specifications** for `open_case` and the assessments.
- **The next batch of actions:** finding and reviewing similar cases and relevant law, the grant decision and the summary.

entries.text: Propose the enabled specifications for open_case, the assessments and reject_application.

I have one option, and the plan passes the check. It adds seven enabled specifications.

- **The six assessment actions:** each is enabled only after `open_case` was executed.
- **`reject_application`:** enabled only after both `verify_certificate` and `check_insurance_membership` were executed.
- **`open_case`:** no enabled specification. It sits on Case, and a Case action can't refer to Application actions such as the robot prechecks.

Two limits to know about:
- The rules about which assessments apply (adult or minor, second caregiver only if there is more than one) aren't covered. They need data conditions, which come later, probably in scenarios.
- `reject_application` can currently be enabled even when the prechecks passed. This needs a data guard, which these conditions can't express.

For reject_application: '{ verify_certificate was executed or is not available AND check_insurance_membership was executed or is not available }'. No enabled specification for open_case, since it is on Case and cannot reference Application actions.", "recommended": true}]}

entries.text: Propose the actions for similar cases, relevant law, review, grant decision and summary.

I split this stage into two options, so each plan stays small enough to review. Both pass the check, and neither adds enabled specifications yet.

**Research and review actions (recommended):** six actions on Case.
- **Similar cases:** `request_similar_cases` (Caseworker, observed by Robot), `find_similar_cases` (Robot, observed by Caseworker) and `review_similar_cases` (Caseworker).
- **Relevant law:** `request_relevant_law`, `find_relevant_law` and `review_relevant_law`, set up the same way.

**Decision and summary actions:** three actions on Case.
- `grant_allowance` is initiated by the Caseworker.
- `summarize_case` is initiated by the Robot.
- `issue_assessment_and_justification` is initiated by the Caseworker and observed by the Citizen.

Each option covers only its own half, so you can approve one and then ask for the other. The ordering rules come afterwards. These include the review blocking the assessments and the grant (a milestone), the summary after the grant, and the justification after the summary.
